title: ImagePipeline Job Spec
description: The universal, provider-agnostic contract for one image-generation job. This is the public API: the same JobSpec drives the CLI today and an HTTP endpoint later. 'Any person's image + prompt' = a JobSpec with reference=<their upload> and spec.prompt_template=<theirs>.

schema_version.description: Contract version. Bump only on breaking changes.

id.description: Slug identifying this job; used in output filenames.

subject.description: Freeform key/value map. Each key is available as a {placeholder} in spec.prompt_template.

spec.description: The FEEDER: the CAD/engineering description + prompt that defines WHAT to render.

prompt_template.description: Prompt with {placeholder} tokens filled from subject + selected output fields ({composition}, {background}).

cad.description: Optional CAD/engineering spec: an inline string OR a path (resolved relative to the job file) to a .md/.txt extraction. Informational; fold into prompt_template as you see fit.

reference.description: The DESIRED TARGET image(s) the engine should match (look anchor). Null/absent for pure text-to-image. String path/URL, object form, or array of either for multi-anchor jobs.

optional.description: If true, a missing reference is a warning not an error.

output.description: The OUTPUT REQUIREMENT — varies case to case. Scalar params map to engine flags; composition/background are folded into the prompt.

imgtype.description: Label used in output filenames (e.g. card, hero, section).

aspect_ratio.description: e.g. 1:1, 4:3, 16:9. Passed to engine when supported.

resolution.description: e.g. 1k, 2k. Passed to engine when supported.

background.description: Freeform background requirement, folded into the prompt (e.g. 'near-black #0b0b0d, floating').

composition.description: Freeform composition requirement, folded into the prompt (e.g. 'upright 3/4 beauty shot').

engine.description: Which generative backend + model. Adapter-selected by name.

params.description: Escape hatch: extra '--name value' flags passed verbatim to the engine.
